content: The moon stays bright when it doesn't avoid the night.
author: Rumi
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. We spend enormous energy trying to present a sanitized, perfect version of ourselves to the world. But whatever emotions or desires we push into the dark don't disappear; they run our lives from behind the curtain.

In Rumi's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. True maturity isn't pretending you have no dark corners—it is having the honesty and courage to look at your jealousy, fear, and anger in the daylight so they no longer control your actions.
reflectionPrompt: When you look back on past hardships, how did navigating them expand your capacity for strength?
